title: Natural long exact sequence from a pair sequence exact on injectives
statement: Let C be an abelian category with injective resolutions [def-sp-abelian, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let A,B,D,E : C → Ab be additive functors and let a:A→B, b:A→D, c:B→E, d:D→E be natural transformations [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Assume for every injective I that x↦(a_I x,b_I x) is injective, its image is the kernel of (y,z)↦c_I y-d_I z, and this difference map is surjective. Then there are natural transformations δ_n:RⁿE→Rⁿ⁺¹A such that for every M and n the sequence RⁿA(M) → RⁿB(M)×RⁿD(M) → RⁿE(M) → Rⁿ⁺¹A(M) → Rⁿ⁺¹B(M)×Rⁿ⁺¹D(M) is exact at the three interior positions. Its two restriction maps use the right derived natural transformations (Rⁿa,Rⁿb) and Rⁿc-Rⁿd. No geometric hypothesis or degree-zero injection is asserted here.

source.place: Tag 0A50, last paragraph, abstracted to four additive functors; Homology Tag 0117

proof.text: Construct the concrete pointwise product functor B×D, the pair map from A and the difference map to E. Their components are definitionally the functions in the hypotheses. Apply the three-functor sequence on injectives to obtain natural boundary maps and three exact pairs.

Use the derived binary product comparison at n and n+1. Its pair and difference equations identify the given restriction maps. Transport the three Function.Exact predicates using bijectivity of the comparison, with injectivity preserving the zero test in the last position.

lean.statement:
theorem rightDerived_pair_sequence
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasInjectiveResolutions C]
    (A B D E : C ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w})
    [A.Additive] [B.Additive] [D.Additive] [E.Additive]
    (a : A ⟶ B) (b : A ⟶ D) (c : B ⟶ E) (d : D ⟶ E)
    (hinj : ∀ (I : C), Injective I →
      Function.Injective (fun x => (a.app I x, b.app I x)))
    (hexact : ∀ (I : C), Injective I →
      Function.Exact (fun x => (a.app I x, b.app I x))
        (fun x => c.app I x.1 - d.app I x.2))
    (hsurj : ∀ (I : C), Injective I →
      Function.Surjective (fun x : B.obj I × D.obj I => c.app I x.1 - d.app I x.2)) :
    ∃ δ : ∀ n : ℕ, E.rightDerived n ⟶ A.rightDerived (n + 1),
      ∀ M : C,
        ∀ n : ℕ,
          Function.Exact (fun x => ((a.rightDerived n).app M x,
            (b.rightDerived n).app M x))
            (fun x => (c.rightDerived n).app M x.1 - (d.rightDerived n).app M x.2) ∧
          Function.Exact
            (fun x : (B.rightDerived n).obj M × (D.rightDerived n).obj M =>
              (c.rightDerived n).app M x.1 - (d.rightDerived n).app M x.2)
            ((δ n).app M) ∧
          Function.Exact ((δ n).app M)
            (fun x => ((a.rightDerived (n + 1)).app M x,
              (b.rightDerived (n + 1)).app M x))
